♡Family Today♡

The storms came through before dawn and are mostly gone by nine; the rest of the day is cloudy, muggy and dry. Bills host Detroit tomorrow at 8:15. Showers are possible during the day but should be finished well before kickoff. The state's first foliage report of the season also comes out this afternoon — see below.
  • Sep 17Bills host Detroit — Thursday night, 8:15
  • Sep 26Harvest Moon, full at 12:48 p.m.
  • Nov 3Election Day
Had a migraine? Say so in the group chat — the day and roughly when — and the paper will mark it on the Barograph. Enough entries and we will know what the glass does before one hits.

Outdoor window Fine from about nine onward, though gray and sticky. Tomorrow has scattered showers through the day, clearing before the eight-fifteen kickoff. Friday is the clean one: sunny, 72, no wind. Pollen Ragweed high.

🍂The Turning🍂

The state's foliage report starts today. For forty years I LOVE NY has sent volunteer spotters out every week to log how far the leaves have turned, and the first of this season's reports lands this afternoon; new ones come every Wednesday until the trees are bare. Niagara County covers North Tonawanda, Chautauqua County covers Dunkirk, Monroe County covers Scottsville.
Numbers here starting tomorrow, refreshed every Wednesday. Nothing has turned yet to speak of — look at the tops of the maples on a back road and you will see the first yellow. North Tonawanda usually peaks in the last week of October.

☾The Almanac Sky☾

Crescent, thirty percent, in Libra, setting at 9:48 — thick enough now to throw a little light. First quarter is Friday afternoon.
Sun 6:56a – 7:23p · 12h 28m · 2h 56m shorter than June 21
Next new moon Sat, Oct 10 · Harvest Moon Sat, Sep 26
Tonight Saturn rises in the east at 8:09 and is up the rest of the night. Jupiter comes up at 3:42 a.m. The equinox is Tuesday at 10:05 a.m. — after that the nights are longer than the days until March.

☰The Barograph · 14120☰

Flat 30.23, down three hundredths, which is nothing. The barometer has been high and steady for three days and stays that way through tomorrow. This is the easy end of the range for your head. The next real move is the weekend, when a wetter system comes in on Saturday.

✶The Ledger✶

A gallon of gas, national average
$4.31
Up sixteen cents in a week, and diesel is still above six dollars. The Gulf is doing this, and it reaches the pump about two weeks behind the barrel — so the sign at the corner has not finished moving.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Supreme Court Blocks the Mail-In Voting Order

The justices halted the administration's restrictions on mail ballots with seven weeks to go. Separately, a whistleblower says federal agents broke the law searching for “unlawful voters.”

2

Trump Calls A.I. Regulation a “Hoax”

The rejection came days after the heads of two major A.I. labs said publicly that development may need to slow down for safety reasons.

3

Iran Says It Downed Two U.S. Drones Over Hormuz

The Revolutionary Guard claimed the strikes as Saudi Arabia's crown prince met the head of Central Command. The ten-year Treasury yield passed 5 percent.

4

New York Leads a Suit Over Immigration Rule

The state heads a coalition challenging the administration's new rule in federal court.

☑ The Ballot · 48 days to Election Day · early voting Oct 24–Nov 1 · register by Oct 24

⛪The Home Wire⛪

1

Dunkirk · Marauders Shut Out Again

Pioneer 35, Dunkirk 0 on Friday night in Yorkshire, the second straight week the team has been blanked. Early turnovers again, and an offense that could not move the ball. Dunkirk is 0–2 in Class B-2.

2

Dunkirk · Assessor Wins in Court

A court has ruled in favor of city assessor Erica Munson — worth watching from here, with North Tonawanda about to reassess every property in the city.

3

Monroe County · Harvest Festival on the 26th

The county's harvest festival is set for Northampton Park on Saturday the 26th, the same day as the Harvest Moon.

★The Marquee★

1

Ed Sheeran's Tour Loses Its Whole Undercard

All four supporting acts — Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Sheeran's own backing band Beoga — quit the U.S. Loop Tour this week after Macklemore was dropped for saying “Free Palestine” onstage at MetLife on September 5.

2

Sheeran Says It Was Not His Call

He posted six slides on Instagram Tuesday saying venues threatened to pull shows if Macklemore stayed, and that the promoter made the decision. Robert Kraft, who owns Gillette Stadium and the Patriots, has confirmed he pressed for the removal and rallied other stadium owners.

3

The Tour Still Has Ten Cities Left

Sheeran plays Gillette Stadium on the 25th and 26th — the venue at the center of the whole thing — with no announced openers and no backing band.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Tomorrow Night at Orchard Park
Bills · Detroit at Orchard Park, tomorrow 8:15 on Prime. Buffalo opened as a two-to-one favorite and the number has not moved. The Lions needed every minute to beat New Orleans 31–30 at home, and they are on the same short week the Bills are. Scattered showers during the day should clear before kickoff.
Jets · Green Bay at the Meadowlands, Sunday 1:00. The Packers are the two-to-one side this time, and they arrive off a 39–22 loss in Minnesota.

⚑The Chase⚑

Three Days to Bristol
Saturday night at 7:30 on USA. Bristol is a half-mile of concrete with corners banked steeper than a highway ramp, which means the cars never stop turning and the tires never stop wearing. Hamlin leads Larson by twelve; Larson won at Gateway on Sunday for the first time in fifty-one races and has run well here before.

☾On This Day☾

September 16, 1620 — the Mayflower left Plymouth with about 102 passengers aboard. The crossing took 66 days; one passenger died and one was born, so the same number stepped off as had stepped on.

✧Question of the Day✧

I turn a whole hillside a different color and take a month to do it, working from the top of the tree down. What am I? Answer below the fold.
Question of the Day: Autumn. The first report of the season is out this afternoon.
